page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton family utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. Running under the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is present via AES extensions, while x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX variants and AMX are not supported on this ARM platform.

Benchmark measurements show strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2337.0, along with exceptional compression metrics, including 36.5 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 17.09 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem also benchmarks in the top 10% under PassMark tests with a score of 3745.62, supported by 120.99 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Multi-core performance is solidly average, scoring 7556.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 8018.98 in stress-ng multi-core testing.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. There are no GPU accelerators present, which restricts deep learning workloads; testing on a 7B parameter LLM resulted in poor prompt processing throughput of 11.27 tokens per second. PassMark overall CPU and encryption scores also test in lower percentiles due to test suite optimizations and architectural differences.

From an operational standpoint, m9g.xlarge offers efficient general-purpose resource density by deploying dedicated ARM cores that eliminate hyper-threading contention. The instance is well suited for web application serving, caching tiers like Redis, microservices, Clang-based compilation pipelines, text processing, and medium-scale backend API hosting requiring reliable single-thread processing efficiency.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 architecture. Managed via the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz with no simultaneous multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates 48 MB of L3 cache and dedicated hardware AES support, though it lacks local NVMe storage and discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional single-core processing capabilities, ranking in the top decile for Geekbench single-core throughput, text processing, and single-threaded data compression. Network bandwidth is configured with a 2 Gbps baseline. Lacking local disks and specialized vector acceleration, the instance delivers predictable per-core execution, making it a reliable fit for containerized microservices, Clang build environments, Redis caching instances, and general web workloads.
